Formulation  
Patient presents with a new unilateral headache associated with visual disturbances, nausea, and vomiting consistent with probable migraine, supported by positive family history. The acute onset and severity have triggered health anxiety/hypochondriasis, with fears of serious neurological conditions such as brain tumor or stroke. No neurological deficits were identified. The patient’s anxiety may perpetuate symptom concern. Protective factors include good engagement and follow-up plans.

Mental Health Care Plan Details  

Principal Problem: Probable migraine with associated health anxiety  
- Patient Goal(s):  
  - Achieve symptomatic relief of headache and associated symptoms  
  - Reduce anxiety related to health concerns  
- Clinical Goal(s):  
  - Confirm diagnosis of migraine after appropriate assessment  
  - Provide effective migraine symptom management  
  - Address and manage health anxiety  
- Actions (Patient):  
  - Trial ibuprofen and anti-nausea medications as advised  
  - Avoid screen exposure and rest with minimal head movement  
  - Attend follow-up assessment for neurological examination  
  - Contact clinic if symptoms worsen or new symptoms emerge  
- Actions (Clinician/GP):  
  - Advise over-the-counter treatment (ibuprofen, antiemetics, sugary/carbonated drinks) for migraine relief  
  - Arrange timely neurological assessment to exclude other causes  
  - Provide reassurance and education about migraine and anxiety  
  - Monitor clinical progress and adjust management as needed  

Secondary Problem: Health anxiety/hypochondriasis  
- Patient Goal(s):  
  - Understand triggers for anxiety and learn coping strategies  
  - Reduce excessive worry about serious illness  
- Clinical Goal(s):  
  - Provide reassurance and education about migraine diagnosis  
  - Support anxiety management, consider referral if anxiety persists  
- Actions (Patient):  
  - Discuss concerns openly during consultations  
  - Utilize coping strategies provided (relaxation, accurate health information)  
- Actions (Clinician/GP):  
  - Educate patient regarding common migraine features and prognosis  
  - Monitor anxiety symptoms; consider referral to mental health services if indicated  

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention  
- Education Given: Yes  
  - Topics Covered: Migraine symptoms, typical course, management strategies, when to seek emergency care  
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Increased headache severity, new neurological symptoms (weakness, speech disturbance), persistent vomiting  
- Coping Strategies: Medication use, avoidance of screens, rest, reassurance about symptom monitoring
